item.title: Refactor orders crate: OrderStatus enum replaces status strings
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim, authenticated local_socket operator instruction):

"The `orders` crate stores an order's status as a `String` and compares string literals all over the code. Refactor it to a proper type:

- Add `src/status.rs` with `pub enum OrderStatus { Pending, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled }` deriving at least `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash`.
- `OrderStatus::as_str(self) -> &'static str` returns the lowercase names ("pending", "paid", "shipped", "cancelled"); `Display` prints the same.
- `FromStr` for `OrderStatus` with `type Err = ParseStatusError`, a public error type that implements `std::error::Error` and whose message names the rejected input.
- `OrderStatus::can_transition_to(self, next: OrderStatus) -> bool` encodes the lifecycle: pending -> paid, pending -> cancelled, paid -> shipped, paid -> cancelled; nothing else.
- `Order::status` becomes an `OrderStatus`; re-export `OrderStatus` and `ParseStatusError` from the crate root; use the enum everywhere, so the status string literals appear only in `src/status.rs`.

Observable behaviour (errors, report output and ordering, parsing) must stay exactly the same, and `cargo test` must pass. Commit your work."

Acceptance criteria:
- src/status.rs exists with the enum, as_str, Display, FromStr (Err = ParseStatusError, public, implements std::error::Error, message includes the rejected input), and can_transition_to exactly as specified above.
- Order::status is OrderStatus; OrderStatus and ParseStatusError are re-exported from the crate root.
- The status string literals ("pending", "paid", "shipped", "cancelled") appear only in src/status.rs (check with grep across the crate, including tests outside src if they are part of the crate, and report any exception).
- Behaviour is unchanged: error messages, report output and ordering, and parsing of existing inputs match the pre-refactor baseline. Characterize before changing where the existing tests do not already cover it.
- cargo test passes; report the output.
- Commit the work on the item's local branch (ship is local; do not push). Commit as the configured git user, no attribution lines beyond what the repository already uses.

Context: this is a behaviour-preserving refactor. Do not add features or change the transition rules beyond the list above.

stages.summary:
BASELINE + CHARACTERIZATION for "Refactor orders crate: OrderStatus enum replaces status strings" (attempt 1, no feedback to address).

STRUCTURAL GOAL (from brief): add src/status.rs with `OrderStatus {Pending, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled}` (Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash), `as_str`, `Display`, `FromStr` (Err = public `ParseStatusError`, implements std::error::Error, message names the input), `can_transition_to` (pending->paid, pending->cancelled, paid->shipped, paid->cancelled only); `Order::status: OrderStatus`; re-export both types from the crate root; status literals only in src/status.rs. Behaviour (errors, report output/order, parsing) must not change.

COMMITS (branch archon/nhdhq0vc-refactor-orders-crate-orderstatus-enum-r, local only, nothing pushed):
- Original baseline: fedb7e0b58e764851abd5e22dc4d2860553f8498 (tree 6e35d20143ea2a04a1a2774dbb91a210c78ccdcf). Production code is byte-identical to this.
- 8232f8c test: characterize status transitions and refusal messages
- a2bb2ca test: characterize report counts, CSV lines and parse errors
- 7c6db09 test: characterize outstanding totals and ready-to-ship order  (HEAD; tree 94ed68c7ea92f1730b00fc1ce0bfca22a4460db8)
Only tests/characterization.rs was added (+285 lines). Author mengsig; no attribution lines, since the repo and CLAUDE.md use none.

CHECKS BEFORE ANY TEST (baseline fedb7e0). No README, CI, Makefile or lint config exists, so the commands come from Cargo.toml (standalone crate, edition 2021):
- `cargo test`: exit 0. 3 tests in tests/orders.rs pass; 0 unit tests; 0 doctests.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets`: exit 0, no warnings.
- `cargo fmt --check`: exit 1. PRE-EXISTING drift, not introduced here: src/billing.rs:2, src/order.rs:23, src/report.rs:15 and :23, src/shipping.rs:2, tests/orders.rs:40. Left untouched because it is out of scope for baseline; the refactorer should decide whether to fmt the files they touch.

CHECKS AFTER ADDING TESTS (HEAD 7c6db09; log published as artifact `baseline-checks.log`, item qi_01M8GVBSV1JNRZWF0YNHDHQ0VC):
- `cargo test`: exit 0. characterization: 21 passed; tests/orders.rs: 3 passed; unit and doc: 0.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0. Clippy first flagged type_complexity on my helper in the third commit; I fixed it with a `type Step` alias and amended that commit before the final run.
- `rustfmt --check tests/characterization.rs`: exit 0. Crate-wide `cargo fmt --check` is still exit 1 with the same six pre-existing diffs.
Build cache: CARGO_TARGET_DIR under this item's cache dir. Nothing started (no servers); the worktree is clean.

PUBLIC-SURFACE INVENTORY (baseline, must be preserved except for the allowed exception):
- lib.rs: `pub mod billing, order, report, shipping`; `pub use order::Order`.
- `Order { pub id: u32, pub customer: String, pub total_cents: u64, pub status: String }`, derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq.
- `Order::new(u32, &str, u64) -> Order` (status "pending"); `is_open(&self) -> bool` (pending or paid); `cancel(&mut self) -> Result<(), String>`.
- `billing::pay(&mut Order) -> Result<(), String>`; `billing::outstanding_cents(&[Order]) -> u64` (sums pending only).
- `shipping::ship(&mut Order) -> Result<(), String>`; `shipping::ready_to_ship(&[Order]) -> Vec<u32>` (paid ids, input order).
- `report::status_counts(&[Order]) -> Vec<(String, usize)>` (sorted by name, present statuses only); `report::to_line(&Order) -> String` (`id,customer,total_cents,status`, no escaping); `report::from_line(&str) -> Result<Order, String>`.
- Exact error strings: "order {id} cannot be paid: it is {status}", "order {id} cannot be shipped: it is {status}", "order {id} cannot be cancelled: it is {status}"; from_line: "expected 4 fields, got {n}", "bad id {:?}: {parse error}", "bad total {:?}: {parse error}", "unknown status {:?}". Validation order is field count, id, total, status.
- No CLI, no binaries, no file format beyond the CSV line.
ALLOWED EXCEPTION (brief): `Order::status` type changes String -> OrderStatus. As a consequence, external code that builds `Order { status: String }` or compares `status` to a literal breaks. Arbitrary status strings also become unrepresentable; the baseline allows them only through the pub field, so I did NOT pin that. The new FromStr/ParseStatusError are additions, not changes.

COVERAGE / WHAT THE 21 CHARACTERIZATION TESTS PIN (tests/characterization.rs):
- Transitions: pay refused for paid and shipped with exact text; ship refused for pending, shipped, cancelled; cancel succeeds from pending and paid; cancel refused for shipped and cancelled with exact text; refused operations leave status unchanged; is_open true for pending and paid only; Order::new fields.
- Report: status_counts order over all four statuses (cancelled, paid, pending, shipped); repeats counted; absent statuses omitted; empty input gives empty. to_line for each status; commas in customer are not escaped and then fail to round-trip ("expected 4 fields, got 5"); from_line round-trips all four statuses; trims outer whitespace only (keeps inner spaces in customer); wrong field counts; bad id/total messages including "", "-1", and u32 overflow; check order id, then total, then status; unknown status is case-sensitive and quoted with Debug (e.g. "Paid", " paid").
- Aggregates: outstanding_cents sums pending only with shipped and cancelled present, and returns 0 for empty input; ready_to_ship returns paid ids in input order (not sorted), and empty input gives empty.
The original 3 tests in tests/orders.rs are unchanged.
Expected-value style: characterization tests read status through Display, and the report comparisons use `.into_iter().map(|(s, n)| (s.to_string(), n))`, so they compile whether status_counts keeps `(String, usize)` or switches to `(OrderStatus, usize)`.

LITERAL-STRING INVENTORY (grep for quoted "pending|paid|shipped|cancelled"):
- Production (src/, 11): billing.rs 3, order.rs 4, report.rs 1 (`KNOWN`), shipping.rs 3. All must move into src/status.rs (or be removed).
- Tests (outside src, part of the crate): tests/orders.rs 4 quoted (lines 10, 12, 14, 43) plus 2 status words embedded in expected error text (lines 23, 26); tests/characterization.rs 16 quoted plus embedded status words in expected error messages.
- EXCEPTION TO DECIDE: the brief's criterion "literals appear only in src/status.rs" cannot hold for test expectations that pin exact error and CSV text. Expected output strings are observable behaviour. My recommendation: allow literals in test expectations only, and have the verifier accept that exception explicitly; otherwise the refactorer must hold the expected text in a way that still pins it, which is not possible without the literal. Decision needed from the orchestrator.

KNOWN GAPS / NOT PINNED:
- outstanding_cents overflow: u64 sum panics in debug and wraps in release. Profile-dependent, so not pinned.
- Mutation testing was not run. Ordering and message tests are the ones most likely to catch regressions.
- The refactorer should watch the decision on status_counts key type (String vs OrderStatus): changing it is a public signature change the brief does not explicitly allow. I recommend keeping `(String, usize)`.

FEEDBACK: none on attempt 1.
FOR THE REFACTORER AND VERIFIER: the bar is `cargo test` exit 0 with 3 original tests and 21 characterization tests passing and unmodified in expected output. Compare against baseline 7c6db09 (or fedb7e0 for production behaviour). Keep clippy -D warnings clean.

Approach: src/status.rs holds OrderStatus (Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash), as_str, Display (uses Formatter::pad so width flags behave as they did for String), FromStr with public ParseStatusError (Display: unknown status followed by the Debug-quoted input; implements std::error::Error) and can_transition_to (pending->paid, pending->cancelled, paid->shipped, paid->cancelled only). Crate-wide cargo fmt --check still reports the pre-existing drift in tests/orders.rs:40, which is left untouched.

Assumptions: status_counts keeps String keys because changing its public signature was not authorised. Test expectations still contain status words, so the literal rule holds for src/ only.

Limits: arbitrary status strings can no longer be set through the public field (allowed by the brief). outstanding_cents overflow behaviour is unchanged and not pinned. No mutation testing run. Nothing pushed.

pr.summary: Order.status is now an OrderStatus enum, not a String. Lifecycle rules are one table (can_transition_to), used by pay, ship and cancel via Order::advance. pr.title: refactor: use OrderStatus enum for order status

risk.why: Public API break, as the brief authorises: Order.status changes from String to OrderStatus, so external code that builds Order with a string status or compares it to a literal will not compile. Other public signatures are unchanged and error text is pinned by tests. The rubric puts API changes that break callers at high. The change is confined to src/ of a small standalone crate and adds no persistence, concurrency or I/O changes. Tests run: cargo test and clippy -D warnings, both passing.
